sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Lavlesh Kumar Sharma Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No. 04 of 2022, under Sections 419, 420, 120-B IPC and Section 66/66D I.T. Act, Police Station Cyber Crime, District Jhansi.

entities.text: Police Station Cyber Crime, District Jhansi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is submitted that in this case applicants are innocent and have committed no offence.
It is further submitted that there is nothing on record to show the complicity of the present applicants in the present case.

It is also submitted that all the offences said to be committed are punishable with Ankit Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119361806/
1 sentence less than 7 years even though the Investigating Officer is trying to arrest the applicants,
therefore, the applicants are under apprehension of imminent arrest.

entities.text: Ankit Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case, the applicants are released on bail, they would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.

Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and urged that in this case all the offences said to have been committed by the applicants are punishable with sentence less than 7 years regarding which protection u/s 41A Cr.P.C. is available to the applicants, therefore, there is no any apprehension of arrest of the applicants by the police.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, it appears that all the offences said to be committed by the applicants are punishable with sentence less than 7 years regarding which protection u/s 41A Cr.P.C. is already available to the applicants, therefore, there may be no apprehension of arrest against the applicants by the police.

Accordingly, this anticipatory bail application is disposed of finally in view of the protection as provided u/s 41, 41A, 60A and interpreted by the Honble Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar (2014) 8 SCC 273 and again reiterated in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another LL 2022 SC 577 decided on 11.07.2022.
